tools.description: Network mapper for host discovery, port scanning, service and OS detection, and NSE scripting. The default scanner; pair with RustScan when you need fast discovery first.
tools.name: Nmap

tools.description: Query registration information (owner, registrar, dates) for domains and IP addresses.
tools.name: whois

tools.description: Enumerate DNS information for a domain: hosts, name servers, MX records, and zone transfer attempts.
tools.name: dnsenum

tools.description: Web server scanner that checks for dangerous files, outdated server software, and common misconfigurations.
tools.name: Nikto

tools.description: Automatic SQL injection detection and exploitation for authorised testing, with database fingerprinting and data extraction.
tools.name: sqlmap

tools.description: Fast network login cracker supporting many protocols (SSH, FTP, HTTP forms, SMB, and more). Use only on systems you are authorised to test.
tools.name: Hydra

tools.description: Offline password hash cracker and hash auditing tool, with a large set of format extractors (the *2john tools). The sensible default cracker on Termux, where there is no useful GPU path.
tools.name: John the Ripper

tools.description: Suite for wireless network auditing: packet capture analysis, WEP and WPA handshake cracking. Capturing needs monitor-mode hardware, which most phones do not provide.
tools.name: Aircrack-ng

tools.description: Extremely fast Internet-scale port scanner. Speed without service detection is not a finished scan; feed its results into Nmap for depth.
tools.name: Masscan

tools.description: Template-based vulnerability scanner from ProjectDiscovery: fast, community-driven YAML templates for known vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and exposures.
tools.name: Nuclei

tools.description: Fast passive subdomain enumeration from ProjectDiscovery, using online sources to map a domain's attack surface.
tools.name: Subfinder

tools.description: ProjectDiscovery's fast HTTP probing toolkit: status codes, titles, technologies, TLS details, and content lengths for lists of hosts. Not the Python library of the same name.
tools.name: httpx

tools.description: Fast web fuzzer written in Go: directory and file discovery, vhost fuzzing, and parameter fuzzing with the FUZZ keyword placed anywhere in the request.
tools.name: ffuf

tools.description: Directory, DNS, and vhost brute-forcing tool written in Go. Simple and predictable; reach for ffuf when you need FUZZ placement inside headers or bodies.
tools.name: Gobuster

tools.description: Network service exploitation and Active Directory assessment tool (SMB, WinRM, LDAP, MSSQL, and more), the maintained community successor to CrackMapExec, which was archived in 2023.
tools.name: NetExec

tools.description: OSINT gathering tool that collects emails, subdomains, hosts, and employee names from public sources for a target domain.
tools.name: theHarvester

tools.description: The curated collection of lists used in security assessments: usernames, passwords, URLs, fuzzing payloads, and web shells, maintained by Daniel Miessler, Jason Haddix, and g0tmi1k. A resource, not a program. The full clone is large; on Termux consider fetching only the lists you need.
tools.name: SecLists

tools.description: Fast recursive content discovery tool written in Rust, with automatic recursion and wildcard filtering. Distributed as a prebuilt binary from the project releases page, so DarkFly lists it as a manual install in Phase 1.
tools.name: Feroxbuster

tools.description: Blazing fast port discovery in Rust that hands open ports straight to Nmap for service detection. Manual install: upstream ships packages and binaries, but there is no maintained Termux route in Phase 1, so it is Linux only here.
tools.name: RustScan

tools.description: Offline search over the Exploit Database archive of exploits and proof-of-concept code, part of the exploitdb package. Manual install in Phase 1: install the exploitdb package from your distribution, or clone the GitLab repository.
tools.name: searchsploit (Exploit-DB)

tools.description: Command-line network protocol analyser from the Wireshark project: capture and dissect traffic in the terminal. Use when you need packet-level detail without a desktop; its GUI sibling is the separate Wireshark entry.
tools.name: TShark

tools.description: The OpenBSD netcat: read and write raw TCP and UDP connections, listen on ports, and pipe data between hosts. Use for quick banner grabs, manual protocol checks, and simple relays.
tools.name: Netcat (OpenBSD)

tools.description: GPU-accelerated password hash cracker with hundreds of hash modes. On Termux there is no useful GPU path, so phone runs are CPU-only and slow: use a laptop with a GPU for real work, and John for quick CPU jobs.
tools.name: Hashcat

tools.description: Python library and script collection for Windows network protocols: secretsdump, psexec, Kerberos tooling, and SMB utilities. Use across Active Directory assessments; installing it exposes the individual scripts.
tools.name: Impacket

tools.description: LLMNR, NBT-NS, and MDNS poisoner for Windows networks: answers name-resolution broadcasts and captures authentication hashes. Needs root and a real lab network, so this entry is Linux-only; DarkFly clones the source, and dependencies and setup stay manual.
tools.name: Responder

tools.description: The Metasploit Framework: exploit development and execution platform. Laptop-class and heavy, with a long install, so DarkFly does not automate it: install on a workstation from the official packages, and avoid the unofficial Termux install scripts, which fetch and run remote code.
tools.name: Metasploit Framework

tools.description: Fast port scanner from ProjectDiscovery with SYN and CONNECT modes and Nmap integration. Use for quick discovery across large target lists before a deep Nmap scan.
tools.name: Naabu

tools.description: Next-generation web crawler from ProjectDiscovery with standard and headless modes and automatic form filling. Use to map a web application's URLs before fuzzing or scanning.
tools.name: Katana

tools.description: Fast DNS toolkit from ProjectDiscovery: resolves, filters, and probes hostnames and records from lists on stdin. Use to clean and enrich subdomain lists inside a recon pipeline.
tools.name: dnsx

tools.description: OWASP Amass: attack-surface mapping through DNS enumeration, external data sources, and infrastructure graphing. Use when a target's full external footprint matters more than speed.
tools.name: Amass

tools.description: Focused XSS scanner and parameter analyser with reflected, stored, and DOM checking modes. Use after crawling or fuzzing has surfaced parameters worth testing.
tools.name: DalFox

tools.description: Fast TCP and UDP tunnel over HTTP, with client and server in one binary. Use to pivot into an internal network segment during post-exploitation.
tools.name: Chisel

tools.description: Kerberos pre-authentication brute-forcing and user enumeration against a domain controller, by ropnop. Use to validate AD password policy and wordlists quickly, with a small footprint.
tools.name: Kerbrute

tools.description: Python ingestor for BloodHound: collects AD users, computers, groups, and sessions over LDAP and SMB. Collector only; the BloodHound server and graph UI run on a laptop.
tools.name: BloodHound.py

tools.description: Offensive toolkit for Active Directory Certificate Services: enumerate templates, request certificates, and abuse misconfigurations. Use on AD CS assessments.
tools.name: Certipy

tools.description: Python WinRM shell for Windows hosts: interactive sessions, file transfer, and service execution once you hold credentials. Use for post-exploitation access on ports 5985 and 5986.
tools.name: evil-winrm-py

tools.description: Advanced XSS detection suite with crawlers, fuzzers, and WAF detection. Installed as a source clone, so review upstream and install its Python requirements yourself before running it.
tools.name: XSStrike

tools.description: Modern rewrite of enum4linux for enumerating Windows and Samba hosts: users, shares, groups, and policy over SMB and LDAP. Needs smbclient on the system path; DarkFly clones the source, and setup stays manual.
tools.name: enum4linux-ng

tools.description: WordPress vulnerability scanner maintained by the WPScan team. Distributed as a Ruby gem, so DarkFly does not automate it: install with the gem route (gem install wpscan) or from your distro, then run it with your own API token.
tools.name: WPScan

tools.description: Secrets scanner that searches git history, filesystems, and cloud storage for leaked credentials, and verifies many key types against their services. Use to audit your own repositories and pipelines.
tools.name: TruffleHog

tools.description: Tunnelling and pivoting tool that exposes a remote network through a TUN interface, with a proxy on your machine and a small agent on the target. Upstream ships release binaries per architecture; DarkFly lists it as manual until a release checksum is maintainer-verified for the binary backend, so download from the project page and check the published sums.
tools.name: Ligolo-ng

tools.description: OWASP Zed Attack Proxy: intercepting proxy and web scanner for desktop use. Desktop companion only: install it on a laptop from the project site; DarkFly will not install GUI tools on this device.
tools.name: OWASP ZAP

tools.description: PortSwigger's intercepting proxy and web security toolkit, the desktop reference for manual web testing. Desktop companion only: download the Community edition from PortSwigger onto a laptop; DarkFly will not install GUI tools on this device.
tools.name: Burp Suite Community

tools.description: Wireshark graphical packet analyser. Desktop companion only: use this entry's CLI sibling, tshark, on Termux and headless Linux, and run the full GUI on a laptop.
tools.name: Wireshark

tools.description: Finds subdomains for a domain from passive online sources, by Tom Hudson (tomnomnom). Use as a fast first pass before heavier enumeration with Amass or Subfinder.
tools.name: AssetFinder

tools.description: Fetches known URLs for a domain from AlienVault OTX, the Wayback Machine, Common Crawl, and URLScan. Use to seed crawling and fuzzing with historical endpoints.
tools.name: gau (getallurls)

tools.description: Identifies the web application firewall in front of a site by sending probe requests and matching responses. Use early in a web engagement so later scans are calibrated.
tools.name: WAFW00F

tools.description: Automated detection and exploitation of command injection vulnerabilities. Use against parameters you are authorised to test when a shell command sink is suspected.
tools.name: Commix

tools.description: Finds hidden HTTP parameters by comparing responses across wordlist-driven requests. Use on endpoints where undocumented parameters may unlock debug or admin behaviour.
tools.name: Arjun

tools.description: Interactive intercepting proxy suite: a console UI (mitmproxy), a web UI (mitmweb), and a scriptable dump mode (mitmdump). Use when you want scriptable interception that also runs on Termux and headless servers.
tools.name: mitmproxy

tools.description: Hunts for a username across hundreds of social networks and sites. Use for OSINT footprinting of your own handles, or an authorised investigation.
tools.name: Sherlock

tools.description: Identifies the algorithm of an unknown hash string, with hashcat and John mode references. Use as the first step before choosing a cracker run.
tools.name: hashID

tools.description: Reads and writes metadata in images, documents, audio, and video. Use to audit what a file leaks (GPS, device, author) before sharing it, or during forensic triage.
tools.name: ExifTool

tools.description: Portable reverse-engineering framework: disassembler, debugger, and binary analysis toolkit driven from the terminal. Use for malware triage and crackme-style work without a desktop IDE.
tools.name: Radare2

tools.description: Multipurpose relay for bidirectional byte streams: files, sockets, pipes, and terminals. Use for port forwarding, quick listeners, and gluing network tools together.
tools.name: socat

tools.description: Reference collection of payloads and bypass techniques for web vulnerability classes, with per-topic notes. A reading and reference resource, not a tool; the clone is your offline copy.
tools.name: PayloadsAllTheThings

tools.description: Large community knowledge base of hacking techniques, privilege escalation, and protocol notes. Read it online at book.hacktricks.xyz; DarkFly does not clone it, because the repository is the book's source, not an offline reader.
tools.name: HackTricks

tools.description: Curated reference of Unix binaries that can be abused to bypass local security restrictions once you have a shell. It is a website, not an install: browse it online when checking a sudo or SUID binary.
tools.name: GTFOBins

tools.description: The rockyou password wordlist, the standard first dictionary for offline cracking labs. Never bundled with DarkFly: download it yourself from a source you trust (the Kali wordlists package, or the copy inside SecLists), expect about 140 MB of plain text, and prefer the smaller SecLists subsets on a phone.
tools.name: rockyou wordlist

tools.description: Modern intercepting proxy written in Rust, positioned as a lighter, faster alternative to Burp with a clean workflow UI. Emerging and desktop-class: install it from caido.io on a laptop; listed so the catalog tracks it.
tools.name: Caido

tools.description: Multi-cloud security auditing tool (AWS, Azure, GCP, and others) that fetches configuration data and produces an HTML findings report. Use to review your own cloud accounts.
tools.name: Scout Suite

tools.description: AWS exploitation framework by Rhino Security Labs: modular post-exploitation and enumeration against an AWS environment you control or are authorised to test. Use it inside a dedicated lab account only.
tools.name: Pacu
